title: Why you should stay natural: permanent gains
summary: NH argues the main reason to stay natural is that natural gains are permanent: natural male hormones peak later than people think, muscle built early carries into old age (his 90-year-old grandfather), and size is retained through layoffs. Muscle gained on PEDs can only be kept on PEDs; ex-users who stay big are on TRT.

claims.claim: PEDs are genuinely tempting for anyone into bodybuilding, so naturals need reasons to resist.
The number one reason to stay natural is that you keep your gains for life, or up to a point.
NH claims natural male hormone levels peak around 35-40, not in the teens or twenties, so a natural lifter's prime comes in the 30s-40s.
Muscle built during your prime remains as hormones decline and protects against disease and injury in old age, which is why doctors recommend strength training early.
NH's grandfather, a construction worker, farmer and hunter for 30-40 years, still wakes at 5am, chops wood and carries logs at 90, which NH attributes to muscle built early and maintained.
NH rejects the idea that building more muscle on PEDs then stopping leaves you better off; science doesn't support it and honest users told him it isn't true.
He has heard that PED use adds muscle cells (muscle memory) and may raise your genetic ceiling permanently, but the dose needed is unknown and still harms health.
Muscle gained on drugs can only be maintained on drugs; once you stop, the hormonal environment disappears and muscles shrink.
Ex-users who say they've stopped and stayed big are on TRT; they are still enhanced, not natural.
As a natural, hormone levels stay stable unless you get very sick, so built mass survives injuries and breaks.
Strength fades much faster than size: when NH stopped training arms for 4-5 months they shrank only a little, and size returned quickly though strength was low.
Enhanced training is a vicious loop: you must stay on drugs to keep the results, suffer lasting health consequences, and lose the work when you stop.
